articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped a historic 200-vulnerability patch bomb, with 36 critical flaws that could probably turn your Windows box into a very expensive paperweight. When Redmond breaks their own records for security holes, you know someone's having a very bad month.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor decided to cosplay as Edward Snowden and dumped AWS GovCloud keys plus a treasure trove of agency secrets on GitHub for the world to see. Congress is now asking the uncomfortable questions that should've been asked before handing government secrets to contractors with questionable operational security.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702's warrantless surveillance authority finally expired, and the EFF is throwing a well-deserved victory party. Because nothing says 'land of the free' like intelligence agencies hoovering up Americans' communications without bothering with that pesky Fourth Amendment.

articles.title: ‘News’ Site Keeps Hallucinating EFF Staffers
articles.summary: California wants to ban 'surveillance pricing' where corporations charge different prices based on your digital stalking profile. Finally, someone noticed that harvesting our browsing habits to price-gouge us might not be the pinnacle of ethical capitalism.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters weaponized an Oracle zero-day to go on a higher education data heist spree, proving that university IT security is about as robust as their student loan forgiveness programs. Nothing says 'ivory tower' like storing sensitive data behind tissue-paper defenses.

articles.title: U.S. Orders Anthropic to Suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Access for Foreign Nationals
articles.summary: Splunk Enterprise users just got a 9.8 CVSS reality check with CVE-2026-20253, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Because apparently searching through your logs shouldn't require authentication when hackers want to add their own entries.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages got hijacked to deploy credential stealers and eBPF rootkits, proving that even the elitist Linux distribution isn't immune to supply chain attacks. Turns out 'I use Arch btw' doesn't automatically confer security superpowers.

articles.title: Show HN: Web Researcher MCP – Search with verify citations and sources
articles.summary: China-linked Velvet Ant group backdoored Linux PAM and OpenSSH for nearly a decade, essentially owning the front door keys to countless systems. While everyone was watching for malware, these folks were rewriting the bouncer list at the club entrance.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Oracle PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Chinese hackers pulled off a decade-long persistence masterclass by hijacking an organization's entire authentication stack with full admin visibility. Ten years of watching every login while defenders played security theater - that's not hacking, that's performance art.

articles.title: Oracle Addresses PeopleSoft Vulnerability Amid Reports of Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary: Oracle's PeopleSoft got absolutely wrecked by hackers who breached 100+ companies using a previously unknown vulnerability that the vendor is still scrambling to patch. When a cybercrime gang starts bragging about your zero-day on social media, you know it's time to update your resume.
